issues.detail: The Greek 'ο ων και ο ην' (the One who is and who was) is translated as 'là Đấng hiện có, đã có' (is the One who exists, has existed). The Vietnamese phrasing 'đã có' implies a completed state of existence in the past, whereas the Greek 'ην' in this context refers to the eternal nature of 'the One who was'. More importantly, the Greek 'ο ων' is typically rendered as 'Đấng là' (The One who is) rather than just 'hiện có' (exists).
